intro.heading: Built on democrito
intro.body: democrito is a token contract, not a component library you are meant to leave alone. Five systems were built on it and measured against base: three shipped products audited against source code, two prototypes read from their design boards. None of them stayed inside the lines. This page records how far each one went, what survived the journey, and — where it matters most — exactly where the contract broke. The failures are published because they are the part worth reading.
intro.note: Divergence is a measure, not a grade. A system further right was pushed harder, not built worse.

systems.name: Southern Startups
systems.tagline: Every startup, investor and programme in Andalucía — in one searchable public directory, with sources

divergence.evidence: components/ui/ holds 5 files against democrito's 48, and none is a retheme. select.tsx is a native <select> where shadcn ships a Radix composite — a different component with a different API and accessibility model. package.json carries exactly one Radix dependency; democrito's primitive layer needs roughly twenty.

systems.headline: Zero base token values survive. It is still recognisably democrito.

--accent.note: renamed --brand. Terracotta → Andalucía green: 127° of hue. The largest single divergence in the set.

--ring.note: ABSENT — replaced by --shadow-focus, a 3-layer composite box-shadow

--radius.note: ABSENT — replaced by a 5-step config-literal scale

systems.tokensInheritedNote: Zero base democrito token values survive unchanged. Every token in the reference set moved value, was renamed, or was deleted. The inheritance here is structural, not chromatic.
systems.renamedNote: The --accent → --brand rename resolved a genuine collision: the authenticated portal inherited 54 shadcn primitives where --accent means 'neutral hover surface', while this codebase used it to mean 'the brand colour'. A usage sweep found ~26 uses meaning hover-surface and zero meaning brand. Rather than repoint either library, the project took --brand — a name neither claims. The cleanest example in the set of a contract break resolved by renaming rather than re-valuing.

themes.note: democrito ships three; this kept one and deleted two. No darkMode key, no ThemeProvider, no prefers-color-scheme block anywhere — a single-theme system with no user choice to make.

absent.consequence: RELOCATED, not absent. Declare both names at the same value or every borrowed component's secondary copy renders at full-contrast ink.
the most dangerous absence — a democrito destructive button renders unfilled and its label as body ink, silently losing the only thing marking it destructive
ring-* compiles to nothing. A borrowed component loses its focus indicator entirely — invisible in screenshots and mouse testing, breaks WCAG 2.4.7 for keyboard users.
bg-primary matches nothing; a default-variant democrito button renders with no background
secondary-variant controls render unfilled — this system's secondary is an outline instead
skeletons and muted panels in borrowed components render transparent
a borrowed dropdown/popover/tooltip renders transparent over page content — unreadable
border-input compiles to nothing; a borrowed input renders edgeless
whole family deleted — a stock sidebar is transparent, unbordered, hoverless
Not declared under democrito's name. Without it a borrowed primary button's label falls back to inherited ink on a brand-green fill — unreadable.
Same gap as --secondary: the role exists as an outline button, the token does not.

systems.recipe: Take democrito's token architecture and directory taxonomy. Keep the storage format and the consumption contract exactly. Replace every value: desaturate the warm surfaces toward neutral, swap the terracotta accent for Andalucía green 127° away, drop to a single light theme. Rename the accent family to --brand to escape a shadcn collision, collapse the three-face type system to two by removing the licence-encumbered body face. Then write your own component layer against the tokens rather than restyling democrito's.

held: The storage format and consumption contract survived a total rewrite of both palette and component layer. A system can share nothing chromatically with democrito and still be structurally the same system.
Zero hardcoded colours across all 34 components — every colour routes through a token, verified by grep.
A naming collision with a foreign library was resolved by taking a third name rather than re-valuing either side. The contract bent without breaking.
broke: ecosystem-map.tsx:47 interpolates var(--status-acquired); the declared token is --color-status-acquired. The class compiles, the declaration is dropped, one of four map markers renders unfilled. The contract held everywhere it was checked and failed where it wasn't.

The focus indicator is declared twice — a custom property in CSS and a hardcoded literal in tailwind.config.ts. They agree today; nothing keeps them agreeing, and the config literal is the one every component actually uses.
Deleting --ring means any borrowed component silently loses its focus indicator — an accessibility failure invisible to screenshots and mouse testing.

whatWeLearned.title: Absent tokens fail silently
whatWeLearned.body: In Tailwind v4 a utility whose token is undeclared compiles to nothing. No error. The class is emitted, the element inherits, and it looks plausible. Observed across all three systems: a flattened surface hierarchy, secondary copy at full-contrast ink, a focus ring that simply isn't there.
evidence: southern-startups: 21 of 31 tokens absent or relocated

whatWeLearned.title: A stock component can be broken by the token layer alone
whatWeLearned.body: habito's sidebar.tsx is byte-identical to shadcn stock and renders transparent, unbordered and hoverless. Nobody edited it. The seven tokens it references were never declared. Its chart.tsx hardcodes .dark, which habito replaced with data-theme — dead code in a file nobody touched.

whatWeLearned.title: The contract stops at the CSS boundary
whatWeLearned.body: Fonts, radius scales, spacing and type scales can reach components through tailwind.config.ts instead of custom properties. Anything supplied by config cannot be re-scoped by CSS — which means it cannot be re-themed by the mechanism democrito is built on.
evidence: prompt-x: all three font families and 26 bare `rounded` classes
habito: spacing, type scale and shadows are Tailwind stock

whatWeLearned.title: Value format is part of the contract
whatWeLearned.body: democrito stores bare HSL triplets consumed as hsl(var(--x)). habito stores complete hsl() at a primitive tier. Both are defensible; they are not interchangeable, and mixing them produces hsl(hsl(0 0% 98%)) — invalid, and silent.

whatWeLearned.title: Naming collisions are real, and renaming is the honest fix
whatWeLearned.body: southern-startups hit a collision where --accent meant 'brand colour' locally and 'neutral hover surface' in 54 inherited shadcn primitives. A usage sweep found ~26 uses of the foreign meaning and zero of the local one. The resolution was to take --brand, a name neither library claims.

whatWeLearned.title: The monochromatic principle needs a carve-out
whatWeLearned.body: prompt-x added 21 hues to encode a 9-field domain model, which reads as a violation of 'monochromatic + accent'. But democrito itself ships a 9-hue --category-* palette. The principle was never written to distinguish decoration from categorical encoding. It should be.

whatWeLearned.title: Nobody did a pure retheme
whatWeLearned.body: Three systems, three verdicts, none of them 'tokens only'. The lightest touch still added 17 components; the heaviest rewrote the primitive layer and kept zero base token values. If the pitch is 'just change the tokens', the evidence says that is not what people do with it.
